tools_helpful.evidence: T44 validator PASS (0 warnings, 0 errors on dotnet build) confirmed the migration was complete before the agent stopped.
T12 the agent fetched windowing + namespace patterns and used them to resolve the TODOs correctly.

tool_limitations.limitation: Reports PASS while dotnet still emits 16 nullable warnings (CS8618/CS8625); the agent had to notice and clean these up manually across turns.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: N/A — warnings are acceptable; the gap is guidance, not tooling.

special_apis.special_handling: Ported unchanged; hardware-gated. With no CO2 sensor present, GetDeviceSelector/FromIdAsync yields no device and the app correctly shows 'No custom sensor found'. No WinUI-specific shim required.

errors_encountered.error: MainPage.g.cs(146,50): error CS0176: Member 'MainPage.FEATURE_NAME' cannot be accessed with an instance reference
errors_encountered.root_cause: XAML used {x:Bind FEATURE_NAME} against a const/static member. x:Bind generates an instance-qualified access path, which is illegal for static/const members.
errors_encountered.fix: Bind to an instance member instead — the agent added 'public string FeatureName => FEATURE_NAME;' and bound {x:Bind FeatureName}. (Alternatively type-qualify: {x:Bind local:MainPage.FEATURE_NAME}.)

errors_encountered.error: SampleConfiguration.cs / Scenario*.xaml.cs: 16x warning CS8618 (non-nullable field/property not initialized) and CS8625 (null literal to non-nullable)
errors_encountered.root_cause: The WinUI 3 scaffold enables <Nullable>enable</Nullable>, but the ported UWP code declared fields like 'private CustomSensor customSensor;' and passed null literals as if nullable were off (UWP projects default to nullable disabled).
errors_encountered.fix: Made deferred-init fields nullable ('private CustomSensor? customSensor;') and null-annotated the null-literal call sites.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: One hard build error CS0176 on x:Bind to the FEATURE_NAME const blocked the first build.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: No skill guidance that x:Bind cannot resolve static/const members via an instance path.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: A note in the MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md x:Bind section that static/const targets need a type-qualified path or an instance wrapper (CS0176).

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: 16 CS8618/CS8625 warnings from ported UWP code under the nullable-enabled scaffold; agent spent extra edit turns annotating fields.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Skill only mentions <Nullable>enable</Nullable> once for a single App.MainWindow field; no general guidance that ALL ported UWP code will trip nullable warnings.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Declared deferred-init fields nullable and annotated null call sites.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: A general nullable-migration note listing the CS8618/CS8625/CS8602 wave and the standard fixes (nullable field for deferred init, null-forgive after guaranteed init).

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Agent produced a malformed constructor while editing scenario files and had to restore it.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Ordinary edit slip, not a knowledge gap.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Agent ran 'winapp build' which does not exist in this winapp CLI version.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Agent assumed a winapp build subcommand; the skill never instructs 'winapp build'.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Fell back to the dotnet build already run by the validator.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: N/A — dev-agent slip; the skill correctly uses native dotnet build.

env_issues.issue: WinUI 3 window screenshots capture a blank white client area (title bar only) due to DirectComposition/PrintWindow limitation.
env_issues.workaround: Verification done via the populated UIA tree + control actuation, not pixels. This is an eval-capture artifact, not a migration defect.
